title: Fast Template Matching for Quantum Circuits Using Hypergraph
authors: Xin Hong, Jintao Yu, Runhong He, Shenggang Ying, Sanjiang Li, Mingsheng Ying
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is a key step toward the efficient execution of quantum algorithms. Template matching has emerged as one of the dominant approaches for simplifying quantum circuits, yet it confronts the intrinsic challenge of accommodating gate commutativity. The state-of-the-art template-matching algorithm relies on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representation. While this DAG-based technique handles gate commutativity satisfactorily, it fails to preserve the local connectivity inherent to quantum circuits, thereby leading to relatively high matching complexity.   In this paper, we introduce a hypergraph representation (HG), a commutativity-aware representation that collapses commuting gates into a single super-node while retaining all local connectivity. This enables matches to be extended locally without revisiting the rest of the circuit, with incremental updates limited to the immediate neighborhood. Experimental results demonstrate that our HG matcher achieves 11--606x speed-up over the DAG-based implementation in Qiskit (Iten et al., 2022) on both random and arithmetic benchmarks, while maintaining the same optimization quality. The acceleration increases with circuit size, confirming that preserving locality and connectivity is the key to scalable quantum circuit optimisation.
summary: This paper presents a novel Hypergraph (HG) representation for quantum circuits to improve template matching for optimization. By collapsing commuting gates into super-nodes while retaining local connectivity, the HG matcher significantly outperforms existing DAG-based methods. This breakthrough promises scalable and efficient circuit simplification for quantum algorithm execution.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently optimizing quantum circuits through template matching while correctly accounting for gate commutativity.
main_result: The proposed Hypergraph (HG) matcher achieves massive speed-ups (up to 606x) over state-of-the-art DAG-based methods on both random and arithmetic benchmarks.
method: It introduces a hypergraph representation that collapses commuting gates into super-nodes while preserving local connectivity, enabling a localized and efficient subgraph isomorphism search for matching.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a quantum circuit, represented as an ordered sequence of quantum gates acting on multiple qubits. The optimization process aims to simplify this circuit structure.
key_observables: Optimization quality (gate count reduction), computational complexity, and execution time (speed-up factor).
important_parameters: Circuit size (number of qubits and gates), and the degree of gate commutation.
main_assumptions: The HG representation is proven canonical only for circuits composed solely of multi-controlled single-target gates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the equivalence of circuits and their representation in the hypergraph format, while tables compare the speed-up and gate reduction achieved by the HG method versus existing DAG-based matchers.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of DAG-based matching, then introduces the HG representation to solve the locality problem, details the HG construction and matching algorithm, and finally validates the approach with extensive experimental comparisons against state-of-the-art tools.
why_interesting: While focused on circuit optimization, the underlying graph theory and the need to efficiently represent complex, constrained relationships (like gate commutation) are relevant to modeling interactions in quantum many-body systems.
